facts.text: TCAS (Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System) warns airline pilots of possible mid-air collisions and advises climbing or descending; ACAS X (Airborne Collision Avoidance System X) is its successor, validated largely by simulation using statistical encounter models of near-collisions.
facts.quote: TCAS is the long-standing system that warns airline pilots of a possible mid-air collision and tells them to climb or descend, ACAS X is its successor, and the encounter model is the statistical description of near-collisions that let ACAS X be validated largely by simulation.

facts.text: TCAS has flown on airliners for decades.
facts.quote: The Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) has flown on airliners for decades.

facts.text: ACAS X chooses its advice from a table computed by optimization.
facts.quote: the Airborne Collision Avoidance System X (ACAS X), chooses its advice from a table computed by optimization

facts.text: ACAS X minimum operational performance standards DO-385 and ED-256, from aviation standards bodies RTCA and EUROCAE, were published in October 2018.
facts.quote: its minimum operational performance standards, DO-385 and ED-256 from the aviation standards bodies RTCA and EUROCAE, were published in October 2018

facts.text: TCAS and ACAS X are advisory systems in which the pilot remains in the loop and flies the maneuver, making them precedents for warning logic rather than automatic braking.
facts.quote: Both systems are advisory: the pilot remains in the loop and flies the maneuver, so they are a precedent for warning logic rather than for automatic braking

facts.text: Aircraft encounter models statistically describe how aircraft come close to each other and are built from years of radar data.
facts.quote: An encounter model is a statistical model of how aircraft come close to each other, built from years of radar data

facts.text: The MIT Lincoln Laboratory aircraft encounter model used nine months of radar recordings.
facts.quote: the MIT Lincoln Laboratory model used nine months of radar recordings

facts.text: The European CREME aircraft encounter model was built based on twelve million flights.
facts.quote: the European CREME model was built "based on twelve million flight[s]"

facts.text: Validation of aircraft collision-avoidance threat-resolution logic involved simulation of close encounters equivalent to billions of flight hours, alongside pilot assessment of individual advisories.
facts.quote: Validation of the threat-resolution logic "involved simulation of close encounters equivalent to billions of flight hours", with pilot assessment of individual advisories alongside.

facts.text: Acceptance of the aircraft collision-avoidance validation came through RTCA and EUROCAE standards and aviation authorities.
facts.quote: Acceptance came through the RTCA and EUROCAE standards and aviation authorities [Chapter 2].

facts.text: March 2022 committee minutes recorded European results suggesting ACAS Xa induced more near mid-air collisions than TCAS, while the US laboratory did not see the same disparity.
facts.quote: in March 2022 committee minutes, European results suggested ACAS Xa induced more near mid-air collisions than TCAS, the US laboratory "didn't see the same disparity"

facts.text: Participants in the March 2022 aircraft collision-avoidance committee discussion noted that sensor noise had not been assessed.
facts.quote: participants noted that sensor noise had not been assessed [Chapter 2].

facts.text: The booklet concludes that ACAS X demonstrates standards-body and regulatory acceptance of statistical simulation as primary evidence for a safety-critical collision function, but only with encounter models built over years from real data and with unresolved disagreements about sensor noise.
facts.quote: ACAS X shows that a standards body and regulators can accept statistical simulation as primary evidence for a safety-critical collision function, but only on encounter models built over years from real data, and even then with unresolved disagreements about sensor noise

facts.text: For the heavy off-road collision-mitigation project, a credible statistical argument needs field data about real interactions first; this is one reason the booklet recommends logging on the existing warning fleet.
facts.quote: For the project, the lesson is that a credible statistical argument needs field data about real interactions first, which is one reason the booklet presses for logging on the existing warning fleet [Chapter 2].
